items.title: crowded-round-introduction
items.claim: In Image #2, the opponent description and input explanation share a large central text panel, while the Techniques button overlaps the fighters’ head-level space.
items.reason: The opening presentation makes instructions, opponent identity, and fighter artwork compete instead of giving the player a clear invitation to fight.
items.suggest: Keep one short opponent tip above the fighters, move the input explanation into Techniques, and place the Techniques control beside the Fight button without covering either fighter.

items.title: reference-sheet-scanability
items.claim: In Image #6, the move list starts only after two direction legends and two explanatory paragraphs, leaving just the first technique group and part of the second visible.
items.reason: A player looking up a move must first scan material that repeats the basic control explanation.
items.suggest: Put a compact stance-plus-technique legend beneath the heading, move scoring details into an expandable section, and provide clearly labeled technique-group tabs above the move list.

items.title: fraction-heavy-score-layout
items.claim: In Image #8, the stacked half-point fraction extends below the adjacent whole-number score in both the top scoreboard and the central result tally.
items.reason: The fraction gives mixed scores a substantially different silhouette from whole scores, making the otherwise simple result display less visually cohesive.
items.suggest: Use a compact inline half-point treatment in both locations, with consistent spacing and alignment; verify the final baseline and bounding boxes in the rendered layout rather than estimating them from this screenshot.

items.title: weak-contact-reaction
items.claim: In Image #12, the scoring kick and contact sparks meet Asmongold’s upper body, but his visible pose remains an upright guard rather than a distinct impact reaction.
items.reason: The contact location agrees with the effect, but the defender’s pose contributes little to the force and clarity of the scoring moment.
items.suggest: Use a dedicated upper-body hit-reaction pose during the scoring presentation, preserving the aligned contact effect and keeping the struck fighter’s face readable.

items.title: settings-panel-crops-fighters
items.claim: In Images #7 and #16, the Settings panel ends across the fighters’ bodies, exposing their lower legs and the arena beneath it.
items.reason: The abrupt crop makes the settings surface feel layered over an unfinished composition rather than deliberately separated from play.
items.suggest: Extend the settings backdrop through the full viewport while keeping the settings content compact, or use a clearly bounded sheet with a uniformly dimmed arena behind it.
